verification.prism_finding_response: PRISM-MTEST-013 (blocker, TEST-5, AC-NFR0159-01, artifact tests/integration/test_server_lifecycle.py) reported the Windows injection as an illegal Red: _windows_driver patched os.name='nt' before the import, so pathlib built WindowsPath, tracks/templating.py's module-level Path(__file__).resolve() raised UnsupportedOperation and the child died with a traceback at 'from tracks.cli.main import main' - it never reached the serve parsing and never produced the contract's unsupported_platform. FIXED: the driver now pre-imports the platform-sensitive standard library (pathlib, shutil, tempfile, subprocess), imports the CLI with the real platform semantics and only then applies the Windows decision the test-plan 6.3 names as the seam (sys.platform + the platform.system override); os.name is deliberately left alone because pathlib decides Path()'s flavour from it at call time and every path the CLI touches would then raise. Both Windows nodes additionally probe the injected CLI with --help first, so a failure under the injection can no longer be confused with a driver that crashes the CLI at import time. VERIFIED at the delivered tree (the implementation-carrying main checkout, the worktree copy restored with git checkout -- afterwards): the injected CLI starts normally (--help exits 0 and prints the usage) and the two nodes now fail on the behavioural contract assertion - 'assert unsupported_platform in trac serve: unknown serve flag: --background' - instead of an import-time traceback.
